CityView – Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

__________________________________________________________________________________

What is CityView?

CityView is your interactive gateway to understanding where and how Bloomberg Philanthropies is driving impact in cities around the world. It integrates data from three primary sources:

  1. BGIVE – For initiative-level activity at the city, state, or country level
  2. BRM – For Highlights submitted by Program Teams, associations, and current/former mayors
  3. Bloomberg Terminal – For cultural access and Bloomberg office locations

_________________________________________________________________________________

What is the goal of CityView?

CityView provides a centralized high-level overview of Bloomberg Philanthropies’ work in a given city or country, enabling stronger context and alignment across teams.

__________________________________________________________________________________

What are teams responsible for adding?

Teams are responsible for adding Highlights. Highlights should summarize key headlines — such as major philanthropic investments, program activities, important announcements, or high-level interactions with senior city officials.

They’re meant to answer the question:

 “What do I need to know before I meet with a mayor or city leader?”

__________________________________________________________________________________

How do I add Highlights to CityView?

Check out the Adding a Highlight to CityView section for a step-by-step guide on how to add and submit a Highlight.

__________________________________________________________________________________

How should Highlights be written? (Style & voice)

  • Length: 1–2 sentences (≈25–60 words). Keep it high-level.
  • No $$: Do not include funding levels or grant terms.
  • Naming: Use “City of X” (e.g., “City of Durham, North Carolina”). Refer to electeds as “Mayor First Last.”
  • Tense & scope: Past tense for completed items (“launched,” “met”); present tense for ongoing work (“is piloting”). One idea per Highlight.
  • Tone: Neutral and factual. Avoid marketing language; use program names.
  • Dates: Don’t repeat dates in the description (they’re captured in fields).
  • Jargon: Minimize acronyms; spell out on first use if needed.
  • Quality: Spell-check and grammar-check before submitting.

Micro-template:

City of [X] [announced/launched/completed/met] [what happened], [why it matters/what it enables].

__________________________________________________________________________________

How long before my Highlight appears in CityView?

Submitted Highlights go through a short review process; most appear within one week, often sooner.

__________________________________________________________________________________

What should I do if my Highlight is time-sensitive?

Enter the Highlight in BRM the same day as the event or announcement, and send an email to bpsalesforceteam@e.bloomberg.org to expedite review and publication.

__________________________________________________________________________________

How do I decide what should be published to CityView vs. logged only in BRM?

  • Log it as an Interaction in BRM only → For general tracking, e.g., “Our team is in touch with this official” — helpful context for colleagues ahead of meetings.
  • Publish to CityView → For front-page headlines: major announcements, strategic milestones, or public-facing updates that reflect our city/country-level impact.

﻿__________________________________________________________________________________

How do I request BRM access for new team members?

Email bpsalesforceteam@e.bloomberg.org and cc the team manager, once approved, the BRM team will coordinate a one-on-one onboarding and training session.

Adding a Highlight to CityView


1. Search for the City

  Use the main search bar in BRM (e.g., City of London).

2. Start a New Highlight 

  On the right-hand side, under Organization Highlights / CityView, click the down arrow and  select New.

3. Complete the Entry Form

  a. Team – Select your team, or the team you're entering on behalf of

  b. Subject, Interaction Date / Start Date

  c. Interaction Type – Select “Program Highlight” (required for CityView)

  d. Description – Include key context and how you'd like it to appear in CityView

  e. Foundation Coding – Use keyword search to find the appropriate code (e.g., Carbon)

4. Submit to CityView

  ✅Check the “Submit to CityView” box — this is required for your entry to be reviewed and published.

5. Save Your Entry

QClick the green Save button at the bottom of the form.


__________________________________________________________________________________


Need Help? 


Contact the BRM team at bpsalesforceteam@e.bloomberg.org with questions about CityView, Highlight submission, or to request additional access.
